headline: Altria’s Interest in Imperial May Affect Its AB InBev Stake
author: Eric Pfanner and Jennifer Creery

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- A possible three-way deal to reshape the global tobacco industry may also spill over into another business whose products are sometimes consumed alongside cigarettes — beer.

That's because Altria Group Inc., the US tobacco company that says it's weighing a bid for Britain's Imperial Brands Plc, holds a roughly 8% stake in Anheuser-Busch InBev. The shareholding dates back to when Marlboro-maker Altria was called Philip Morris and owned Miller Brewing Co., one of the companies that evolved into the world's largest brewer after a series of deals.
To finance a deal for Imperial, likely in partnership with Japan Tobacco Inc., Altria may sell some or all of its stake in AB InBev that's worth $12.8 billion, Jefferies analysts said.

"Altria has suggested before in the past that it's something that's worthy to generate cash at any given need and that it would be open to trimming or selling altogether," Jefferies analyst Andrei Andon-Ionita said by phone.

The knock-on effect could then see AB InBev buying back a portion of this holding, analysts at Jefferies said in a note, just as it did when Altria reduced its stake from 10% about two years ago. Doing so could modestly boost AB InBev's earnings per share but also raise its debt ratios, they wrote.
The brewer had no immediate comment when contacted by Bloomberg.

AB InBev could buy back as much as $10 billion of this stake while keeping net debt at 2.9 times earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, the analysts wrote, based on the current expected leverage of 2.5 times in its fiscal year starting in January. "However we would anticipate a more modest participation in the event of a selldown," they said.

AB InBev shares traded lower on Thursday after Bloomberg reported the interest in Imperial and Altria said it was weighing a cash offer for the tobacco company. They were down as much as 1.2% in Brussels on Friday.

For Altria, selling a portion of its stake could affect its representation on AB InBev's board, which was reduced from two seats to one after the 2024 reduction in its shareholding, the analysts said.
